title: Auth Control Plane service account token (v1 wire format)
description:
The service account token the auth-service signs for one service account key (credential class `service_account_token`): a compact JWS whose protected header and payload, decoded, are the two members of this document. The signature is not part of the document; a verifier checks it with the issuer's jwks.v1 key named by `kid`, and the signed bytes are decided by the golden corpus under golden/service-account-token.

A service account token is its own type and its own shape. Its header typ is `sa+jwt` (RFC 8725 explicit typing), exact bytes, so it can never be read as a user access token (`at+jwt`), a workload token (`workload+jwt`), an ID token or the HS256 token (`JWT`). It names exactly one audience, `dev-health-api`, the only audience whose classes in contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/audiences.json include `service_account_token`. It names the account (`sub`), the account's organization (`org_id`) and the key row the exchange read (`cid`), so a relying party re-checks the live state of both. It has no `sid`, no `scope` and no audience list: a service account has no session, and nothing in the token grants a permission. Its lifetime is at most 300 seconds (a client rule, ServiceAccountTokenLifetimeCeiling) and never past the key's expiry (ServiceAccountTokenLifetime): a verifier refuses a longer one even when the signature is valid.

header.description: The JWS protected header. Closed: a verifier never reads a key, key URL or certificate from the token.

alg.description: Ed25519 only (ACP-ADR-01). A verifier fixes this before it resolves a key.

typ.description: RFC 8725 explicit type, exact bytes. A verifier refuses a case variant, a missing typ, `JWT`, `at+jwt`, `workload+jwt` and an `application/`-prefixed form. It separates this token from the user access token (`at+jwt`) and the workload token (`workload+jwt`).

claims.description: The JWT claims. Closed to the account, its organization, the key row and the validity window: no session, no scope, nothing that grants a permission.

aud.description: Exactly one audience: dev-health-api. contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/audiences.json lists every audience and the classes that may carry it; only this one lists service_account_token.

principal_type.description: A service account token names a service account principal. A human principal holds a user access token and a workload a workload token.

org_id.description: The organization of the service account, as a lowercase UUID. Context, not proof: a relying party reads the live account row and never trusts this claim over it.

cid.description: The credential registry row id of the key the token was exchanged for (the wire form of credential-entry.v1 id). A relying party refuses the token at once when that key is revoked or expired.

numericDate.description: Seconds since the epoch (RFC 7519 NumericDate), no later than 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z.
